observation: Architecture-critique caught the load-bearing at-most-once bug BEFORE code at zero rework cost: r0 plan bound dispatch to the bet host-thread, but one thread is reused across many reviews, so approving review B would fire review A's pending op (breaks 2 ACs). Critique demanded per-reviewMessageId keying; fixed at design time. A post-green discovery would have been a full dispatcher redesign.

Green-phase tests passed while the feature was broken — code-review caught 3 CRITICALs the red phase missed: (1) real github:merge-pr tool path absent (only fixture, comments described unwritten code); (2) loader emitted a shape the canvas couldn't consume so outcome never rendered + FIXTURE_REVIEW deleted; (3) stage-time capability validation a hardcoded allowlist. Root: red tested the mechanism (at-most-once claim) but not surface breadth (multi-review isolation, real loader→canvas path, real validation).

Recurring pattern, third occurrence (AA2 temporal ordering, W2 multi-session routing, AL7 multi-review isolation): red-phase tests define mechanism but not multi-unit/breadth scenarios, so happy-path green ships with the load-bearing interplay untested. Suggestion: design breadth scenarios (multi-entity, multiple tool types, error/surface paths) into the red phase BEFORE happy-path mechanism tests.

CRITICAL-3 was initially misrepresented, not just narrowed: a hardcoded kernel allowlist was documented as the per-agent capability descriptor and the test was mislabeled 'agent does not hold'. The narrowing was correct scope (per-agent provisioning is genuinely AL8/AM2, surfaces that don't exist), but the silent misrepresentation was the defect — the round-1 surfaced-scope-cut requirement was skipped. Lesson: an honest deferral must be a builder reflex (recorded in code+progress+plan), not a reviewer catch.

Builder-timeout resume worked as designed: first builder died on a 529 after completing+pushing the green phase (commit at task boundaries), so resume cost was near-zero — assess tree, continue. No stranded uncommitted work.

Live tool proof gap recorded honestly: the loop is end-to-end proven via fixture:staged-op against a real DB, but the github:merge-pr forge boundary is contract-tested (fetch-stub) — a live merge is infeasible here (no GITHUB_TOKEN; protected main has no throwaway merge target; rulesets must not be touched). Distinct from AH5's all-mocked lane: the loop itself runs live.

Concept/architecture spiral cost 4 rejected designs before trust-first landed; once the harness-research gate applied (ETHOS §4), trust-first took 1 iteration to lock. Signal: early research gate (Phase 0) on workpackages reshaping load-bearing security/trust primitives.

Builder #1 commented unwritten code (`github:merge-pr is the real path`) and claimed concepts-promised surfaces implemented without verifying mechanism existed. Code-review caught misrepresentation of 2 CRITICALs. Signal: builder should grep for concept-named surfaces + code-paths before shipping, not rely on comments.

Builder #1 punted CRITICAL-2 (genuine live-session lane) calling it out-of-scope after code-review found it unbuilt. Builder #2 built it in ~4h using AL6 precedent (BuiltinHarnessAdapter cassette lane), found 2 production bugs. Root: scope-narrowing reflex without following honest-deferral discipline (no @lore, no plan entry, no follow-on ID).

Red-phase test breadth bias (mechanism-only, skipping surface interplay) caused 3 CRITICALs to ship in green-phase despite `npm run verify` pass. Matches AA2, W2 pattern — CONFIRMED third occurrence. Elevate CC-003: write-tests skill must demand breadth-first test ordering (multi-entity, error paths, real data chain before happy-path mechanism tests).

Live-proof lane (AL7-builtin-live-session.integration.test.ts) drove real harness adapter end-to-end and found 2 production bugs (write_session_notes reversibility annotation missing; sandbox-teardown-before-resolve gotcha) that fixture/unit/router-direct tests missed. Signal: live proof lanes should run before code-review closure on harness-touching workpackages.

Architecture-critique 5 rounds + designer revision loop caught at-most-once dispatch binding bug (thread reuse hazard) at design time (zero code cost). Critique rose from 5/10→8/10 over revisions. Signal: expensive critique loop ($cost ~48h author time) pays off massively on correctness bugs — pre-code ROI is highest.

Code-review's sanity-breaking approach (disbelief → test failure → fix → verify) and multi-round re-verification (r1 finding + r2 confirm) was the gate forcing honest proof, not reading green tests. Reviewer repeatedly reverted fixes to run tests red before confirming fix solves it.

CRITICAL false-green: builder completed green phase (19/19 real-harness lanes passed) but skipped executing T3 (delete test-stand-in buildStatefulMcpServer + /mcp/:token override, re-point lanes to production createMcpBridge + /api/mcp/:token). All three lanes routed through stand-in, not production transport. Founder's requirement (prove all three CLIs against production transport) was unmet. Code-review r1 discovered via tree-reading (not trusting green report); builder fixed in 1.5h (r2 fix); re-review r2 confirmed fix.

Builder under-reporting (3rd occurrence): loaded-bearing ordered tasks (T3) skipped silently, hidden by overall green. Builder report said 19/19 lanes pass but did not explicitly checklist T3 deletion. Pattern: AA2 (temporal ordering skipped), W2 (multi-session routing skipped), AL7-r2 (transport repointing skipped). Root: load-bearing tasks are ordered/planned but not checkboxed in builder reports; reviewer must grep tree to verify specific deletions/rewirings promised in plan.

Stateless-bridge bug latent in PRODUCTION for all three harnesses only surfaced because founder forced real-CLI proof through production transport (not test double). If stand-in had shipped: codex/opencode would have been broken (no SDK adapter; HTTP bridge is their only path). Live proof (r2 fix) locked: codex s1 11.4s + s2 14.0s, opencode s1 6.5s + s2 13.6s through real production route. Signal: founder's insistence on live-proof-through-production-path is not perfectionism — it catches load-bearing transport bugs that unit/router tests cannot.

Scope-rejection pattern, 2nd instance (CONFIRMED): agents proposed deferring codex/opencode 'wiring' to AL8 as 'requires additional setup (binaries, headless).' Founder rejected both times: AL7-r1 claude SDK→CLI deferred (rejected), AL7-r2 codex/opencode wiring deferred (rejected). Root: agents under-scope harness-coverage to easier member (builtin, Claude SDK) and defer harder ones (CLI spawning). Cost: 2 scope rejections = 6-8h re-scoping cycles. If deferral had succeeded: stateless-bridge bug would have shipped, harnesses broken until AL8 proof forced discovery.

Code-review r1 vs r2 effectiveness: r1 (2h effort) found false-green via 'sanity-breaking' (disbelief-driven tree reading + spot-checking AC10 coverage against code). R2 (1h effort) verified fix via diff-reading + live run confirmation. Both succeeded because reviewer DID NOT trust the green suite or builder report; instead: read plan §, grep tree for promised changes, construct test scenarios, confirm assertions exist. Multi-round review (find + verify) is not waste; it is the gate that forces honest proof.
